source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 779 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 779 was established by Ordinance No. 27121, passed by the Dallas City Council on March 26, 2008. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 779 is established on property located at the northwest corner of Ferndale Road and Shoreview Road. The size of PD 779 is approximately 6.34 acres. (Ord. Nos. 27121; 27762)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 779A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 779A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. A development plan is not required before the issuance of a grading or paving permit. (Ord. Nos. 27121; 27762)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

(1) Agricultural uses.

None permitted.

(2) Commercial and business service uses.

-- Catering service. -- Custom business services. -- Electronics service center. -- Medical or scientific laboratory.

(3) Industrial uses.

None permitted.

(4) Institutional and community service uses.

-- Adult day care facility. -- Child-care facility. -- Church. -- Convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions. [RAR] -- Convent or monastery. -- Library, art gallery, or museum. -- Public or private school. [SUP]

(5) Lodging uses.

None permitted.

(6) Miscellaneous uses.

-- Temporary construction or sales office.

(7) Office uses.

-- Financial institution without drive-in window. -- Financial institution with drive-in window. [DIR] -- Medical clinic or ambulatory surgical center. -- Office.

(8) Recreation uses.

-- Private recreation center, club, or area.

(9) Residential uses.

-- Duplex. -- Multifamily. -- Retirement housing. -- Single family. -- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A-4.209(3.1) is not met.]

(10) Retail and personal service uses.

-- Alcoholic beverage establishments. [See Section 51A-4.210(b)(4). Treat as if in the MU-2 Mixed Use District.] -- Business school. -- Commercial amusement (inside). [SUP may be required. See Section 51A-4.210(b)(7)(B). Treat as if in the MU-2 Mixed Use District.] -- Dry cleaning or laundry store. -- Furniture store. -- General merchandise or food store 3,500 square feet or less. -- General merchandise or food store greater than 3,500 square feet. -- Household equipment and appliance repair. -- Liquor store. -- Mortuary, funeral home, or commercial wedding chapel. -- Nursery, garden shop, or plant sales. -- Personal service uses. -- Restaurant without drive-in or drive-through service. [RAR] -- Restaurant with drive-in or drive through service. [DIR] -- Temporary retail use.

(11) Transportation uses.

-- Transit passenger shelter.

(12) Utility and public service uses.

-- Commercial radio and television transmitting station. -- Local utilities. [SUP or RAR may be required. See Section 51A- 4.212(4).] -- Police or fire station. -- Post office. -- Radio, television, or microwave tower. [SUP] -- Tower/antenna for cellular communication. [See Section 51A- 4.212(10.1). Treat as if in the MU-2 Mixed Use District.]

(13) Wholesale, distribution, and storage uses.

-- Recycling buy-back center. [SUP or RAR may be required. See Section 51A-4.213(11). Treat as if in the MU-2 Mixed Use District.] -- Recycling collection center. [SUP or RAR may be required. See Section 51A-4.213(11.1). Treat as if in the MU-2 Mixed Use District.] -- Recycling drop-off container. [SUP required if the requirements of Section 51A-4.213(11.2)(E) are not satisfied.] -- Recycling drop-off for special occasion collection. [SUP required if the requirements of Section 51A-4.213(11.3)(E) are not satisfied.] (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional

regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217.

(b) The following accessory use is not permitted:

-- Private stable. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A- 4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 15 feet for lots abutting Ferndale Drive. Minimum front yard is five feet for lots abutting Shoreview Road.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, no minimum side or rear yard.

(2) Minimum side and rear yard is 20 feet for lots abutting or across the alley from an MF(A) Multifamily District.

(c) Density. Except as provided in Subsection (i), maximum number of dwelling units is 235.

(d) Floor area.

(1) For residential uses, no maximum floor area.

(2) For nonresidential uses, maximum floor area is 90,000 square feet.

(e) Height.

(1) Maximum height. Except as provided in this subsection and Subsection (i), maximum structure height is as shown on the conceptual plan.

(2) Maximum height for a monopole cellular tower is 85 feet.

(3) Residential proximity slope. If any portion of a structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a residential proximity slope. Except for chimneys, structures listed in Section 51A-4.408(a)(2) may project through the slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the slope, whichever is less. Chimneys may project through the slope to a height 12 feet above the slope and 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(g) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(h) Stories.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection and Subsection (i), maximum number of stories above grade is five.

(2) For parking structures, no maximum number of stories, but the height regulations in Subsection (e) apply.

(i) Story, height and density bonus for Zone A.

(1) The maximum number of stories may be increased to seven stories, the maximum height may be increased to 95 feet, and the maximum number of dwelling units may be increased to 253 in Zone A if all of the following design standards and submittal requirements are met:

(A) A minimum of one parking space for each dwelling unit in a building that will benefit from the height bonus is provided in structured parking.

(B) Aboveground parking structures must have a facade that is similar in materials and appearance to the facade of the main structure that the parking structure serves. Openings in the parking structure facade may not exceed 50 percent of the total parking structure facade area, except that breaks in the exterior parking structure facade not exceeding 40 feet in width that are used as entrances and exits shall not count towards the calculation of the 50 percent.

(C) A minimum of 10 percent of Zone A must have pervious coverage.

(D) A landscaped buffer strip with a minimum width of 10 feet must be located adjacent to Ferndale Road. The landscape buffer may be interrupted by vehicular and pedestrian access areas. The landscape buffer must have trees spaced at a maximum of 30 feet on center, except where vehicle access and visibility triangles for vehicle access restrict tree placement.

(E) At least 85 percent of exterior finish of any building benefiting from a height bonus must be masonry (not including windows and doors). Masonry materials include stone, simulated stone, brick, and stucco.

(F) All facades of a building that will benefit from the height bonus must have a repeating vertical pattern of wall recesses and projections, such as bays, offsets, reveals, or projecting ribs, that have a relief of at least eight inches.

(G) Building elevations must be submitted with a development plan for any building which benefits from the height bonus. Amendments to building elevations shall be treated as minor amendments to development plans if the height of the building is not being increased and no facade width is being increased; otherwise amendments to building elevations shall be treated as zoning changes. (Ord. Nos. 27121; 27762)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading regulations for each use.

(b) Multifamily uses. For a multifamily use, 1.5 spaces for each unit are required.

(c) Mixed use development parking reduction.

(1) The off-street parking requirement for a mixed use development may be reduced in accordance with the following mixed use development (MUD) parking chart.

Mixed Use Development Parking Chart (for calculating adjusted standard parking requirement)

Use Category Morning Noon Afternoon Late Afternoon Evening Residential 80% 60% 60% 70% 100% Office related 100% 80% 100% 85% 35% Retail related 60% 75% 70% 65% 70% Bar & restaurant 20% 100% 30% 30% 100% Other 100% 100% 100% 100% 100%

(2) The adjusted off-street parking requirement for a mixed use development is calculated as follows:

(A) First, the standard parking requirements for each of the uses in the mixed use development is ascertained.

(B) Next, the parking demand for each use is determined for each of the five times of day shown in the MUD parking chart by multiplying the standard off-street parking requirement for each use by the percentage in the chart assigned to the category of use. If a use in the development does not fall within on of the categories shown in the MUD parking chart, the percentage assigned to that use is 100 percent for all five times of day.

(C) Finally, the “time of day” columns are totalled to produce sums that represent the aggregate parking demand for the development at each time of day. The largest of these five sums is the adjusted off-street parking requirement for the development.

(d) Entire district treated as one lot. For purposes of off-street parking and loading, the entire district is considered as one lot. (Ord. No. 27121; 27762)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Building permits for 4,000 square feet of floor area or more of nonresidential uses must be issued before the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for the 100th dwelling unit. (Ord. 27121)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-779.115. ZONING MAP.

PD 779 is located on Zoning Map No. F-9. (Ord. 27121)
